newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-KLINSMANN, BAYERN MAY REGRET MISSES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-KLINSMANN, BAYERN MAY REGRET MISSES.

text.p: If Juergen Klinsmann was banging in the goals with the confidence he has shown at World Cups in the past, Bayern Munich would be running away with the German league championship.
But the German national team captain and striker is not at his best and neither are Bayern.
The Bavarians played some entertaining football and created a handful of chances in Sunday's 0-0 draw with reigning champions Borussia Dortmund in Munich.

But Klinsmann was unable to score the vital goal to clinch three points and is lacking the sharpness which made him one of the most prolific strikers at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups and at this year's European championship.
After 11 games Bayern are level on points with leaders VfB Stuttgart and four points ahead of Dortmund who are fourth after stuggling with injuries for most of the season.
But Bayern should have won Sunday's game after outplaying their opponents for long perids. Klinsmann knows he must carry part of the blame.
"We had -- No, I had -- enough chances to clinch the game," the former Tottenham forward said. "That is annoying and that is why I am not happy with the result."
Bayern played some entertaining football on a cold, damp night and midfielder Mario Basler was outstanding with his creative running and passing.
But the Munich club were unable to find a way past Dortmund's excellent goalkeeper Stefan Klos who is pushing for a place in the German national squad.

Despite their overall superiority, Bayern lacked composure in the penalty area. They could regret dropping the points at the end of the season when Dortmund are sure to make a serious challenge after their problematic start.
"We have not reached the level we want to," said Bayern captain Lothar Matthaeus.
Chairman Franz Beckenbauer added: "Juergen tried hard and created chances but he was unlucky. You get days like that when things don't go right."
Dortmund have had an array of injury problems and are still without key libero Matthias Sammer -- Germany's most influential player at Euro 96.
Yet, despite the setbacks, they are almost certain of a place in the quarter-finals of the European Cup and are happy to be only four points behind the leaders in the Bundesliga.
German international midfielder Andy Moeller, who returned against Bayern after a leg muscle injury, believes the difficult days could soon be behind the Ruhr team.
"The result was very important. We are in the race," Moeller said. "If we had lost in Munich it would have hurt because we would have been seven points behind."
